findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored without KMS-backed encryption. This bucket receives a customer master data file, so sensitive PII is persisted unencrypted at the bucket-policy level.

No ACL is declared and no companion aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource exists to block public ACLs or public bucket policies; the inline comment '# bucket is public' documents the intent that this bucket be publicly readable. Anyone able to set an ACL or bucket policy can expose the customer master file to the internet.

A file containing customer master records is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument, into a bucket that also lacks default encryption and public-access controls. The sensitive object is stored in cleartext and is at risk of exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket named to hold financial records, so objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so data science datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest, unlike the logs bucket which correctly uses aws:kms.
Reliance on the private ACL alone leaves no defence in depth: there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block to prevent a later public bucket policy or ACL change from exposing financial data.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block accompanies this bucket, so account- or bucket-level public policies and ACLs are not blocked, leaving the private ACL as the only control.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block accompanies this bucket, so nothing prevents a subsequent public ACL or bucket policy from exposing its contents.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects including the customer master file can be read or written over unencrypted HTTP.
No bucket policy enforces TLS via a aws:SecureTransport condition, so financial data may be transmitted to and from the bucket over plaintext HTTP.
The logs bucket encrypts at rest with KMS but has no bucket policy requiring aws:SecureTransport, so audit log objects can still be retrieved over unencrypted HTTP.
